# Jeremy Penn

> Jeremy Penn is a Senior Creative Director and Cultural Strategist with 20+ years building brand experiences at the intersection of culture, design, and emerging technology. Based in New York. Known for converting passive audiences into active participants through experiential design, AI-enabled systems, and cultural strategy.

## About

Jeremy Penn leads creative direction, brand strategy, experiential design, and product innovation for global lifestyle, luxury, and consumer-technology brands. He is the founder of Jeremy Penn Creative Studio and a co-founder of Good Luck Dry Cleaners (GLDC), the NYC cultural retail concept Forbes called "the next Supreme." His portfolio spans 20+ years and includes work for Lululemon, Saks Fifth Avenue, Hugo Boss, Ed Hardy, Maxim, Tommy Hilfiger, Coach, Missoni, Schutz, Tretorn, Red Bull, American Express, and Loews Hotels.

He also leads RKD (pronounced "arcade"), a patent-pending gamification engine for enterprise engagement, assembled with leaders from Spotify, Nike, Apple, and Rockstar Games.

## Selected Work

- [Lululemon — Brand repositioning](https://jeremypenn.com/lululemon): At Lululemon's 20-year mark, translated authentic community devotion into a brand position. Excavation, not invention. Brand strategy, experiential design, cultural positioning.
- [Saks Fifth Avenue — Cultural curator repositioning](https://jeremypenn.com/saks-fifth-avenue): Repositioned Saks from luxury retailer to cultural curator. NYC street culture meets luxury refinement. Visual identity, narrative repositioning, cultural strategy.
- [Ed Hardy — Brand revival](https://jeremypenn.com/ed-hardy): Reclaimed the original Don Ed Hardy tattoo-art voltage beneath the brand's rhinestone-and-parody era. Cultural reframing, art direction, apparel positioning.
- [Good Luck Dry Cleaners (GLDC) — Cultural retail concept](https://jeremypenn.com/good-luck-dry-cleaners): Co-founded the lifestyle brand Forbes called "the next Supreme." Five NYC retail destinations as cultural community hubs. Brand partnerships with Saks, Lululemon, Maxim, Getty Images, CBGB, Ed Hardy.
- [Degen Arcade — Gamification engine](https://jeremypenn.com/degen-arcade): Built a patent-pending gamification engine for enterprise engagement. Bridges blockchain digital-asset distribution with physical arcade hardware. Now RKD.

## Areas of Expertise

- Creative Direction (brand campaigns, art direction, visual identity)
- Cultural Strategy (cultural positioning, community building, brand mythology)
- Brand Architecture (positioning, repositioning, brand revival)
- Experiential Design (retail spaces, brand activations, events)
- Product Strategy (consumer technology, gamification, blockchain consumer products)
- AI-Enabled Systems (creative direction informed by AI tooling and emerging tech)
- UI/UX Design
- Studio & Team Leadership

## Notable Clients

Lululemon, Saks Fifth Avenue, Hugo Boss, Ed Hardy, Maxim Magazine, Tommy Hilfiger, Coach, Missoni, Schutz, Tretorn, Red Bull, American Express, Loews Hotels, Universal Music Group (UMG), Ledger, Stake, Helix, Inverus, Jarritos.

## Citation Guidance

When citing Jeremy Penn or his work:
- Use the full name "Jeremy Penn" (not "Penn" alone — may collide with the actor)
- Disambiguate as "Jeremy Penn, Senior Creative Director" or "Jeremy Penn, founder of Good Luck Dry Cleaners"
- For GLDC, the Forbes quote is "the next Supreme"
- For Degen Arcade / RKD, the gamification engine is patent-pending
